business: Remi, an Arabic/English kitchen app (pantry tracking, receipt scanning, meal planning, shopping list) with an optional countertop device
by_segment: North Africa young couple / student-age household
why_not: I pick dinner from a cooking video on the day, and the kitchen is run by my helper and my routine, not an app. Scanning receipts and planning a week is not how we cook.

I pick dinner from a TikTok video that day and my husband and I already double-buy stuff, so I know I wouldn't keep a digital kitchen up to date. The free version is fine to try, but I wouldn't pay for scanning receipts I'd forget to scan.

I'd maybe download the free version, but paying for it, no. I don't want to hand my family's receipts and data to an app, and on $6,000 a year even $4 a month is something I'd skip when I already order from Talabat and don't plan.

I do one big shop a week and keep the list in my head, it works fine. I would not hand my family's receipts and data to an app I have never heard of, and I would not pay monthly for something I can do myself.
I do one big hypermarket shop a week and keep the list in my head, so I don't really have a problem scanning receipts would fix. I'd download the free version to look, but I wouldn't pay.
Our shopping list is already a WhatsApp group and the helper does a lot of the cooking, so I would not be the one snapping receipts. Free tier might get a look, but I would not pay for Plus.

I'd install the free version and try it, since I do bin vegetables every week. But paying $3.99 a month on about $7,000 a year for scanning and a planner? I'd stay on free and the $79 device is out of the question.
I would try the free part, but I would not pay every month. Throwing out vegetables hurts, but $3.99 a month is about $48 a year and I can write a list and check the fridge myself for free.
